clue.text: Officer playing rotten old horn

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters perform in a new arrangement, so the word rotten is jumbled

explanation.surface: An officer is making a hash of an old brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' seems to belong with the horn as music-making, but it is the anagram signal, giving RNETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornett is a Renaissance wind instrument, and this Italian spelling names that historical horn.

clue.text: Accident to an extent interrupting plan

indicators.note: interrupting means one piece breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart of an area
the suffix -ish means somewhat, to an extent

explanation.surface: A partial accident has disrupted the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is a minor accident or unlucky event, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: How post gets around vegetable market, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words are exchanged by sound

parts.note: kale is a leafy green vegetable
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A description of how the post travels round a greengrocers' market.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of KALE MART gives a 'mail cart', spelt by sound rather than letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail cart is a vehicle that carries letters and parcels, so it is how post travels about.

clue.text: Clergyman to go off with fool to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: food that goes off will rot
a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A clergyman is told to run off northwards with a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns ROTSAP around in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister in charge of a congregation, a synonym for clergyman.

clue.text: Writer pockets tenpence piece in the cinema

indicators.note: pockets means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, something that writes
10p written with I and O for the digits

explanation.surface: A writer slips a ten-pence coin into a pocket at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tenpence piece' looks like one coin, but 'piece' belongs to the definition: a film is a piece shown in the cinema. 10P is read as letters IOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopic is a biographical film, so it is a work screened in picture houses; the word blends biographical and picture.

clue.text: Carried nothing in island

parts.note: borne is the past participle of bear, to carry
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Something with nothing was transported to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large island in Southeast Asia, shared by three countries.

clue.text: Ally in war zone shows weapon there

indicators.note: in means the ally sits within the war zone's letters

parts.note: 'Nam is slang for Vietnam, scene of the Vietnam War
a pal is a friend or ally

explanation.surface: An ally in a war zone displays a weapon used in that conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to Vietnam, where the incendiary was notoriously used, making the definition specific to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is an incendiary jelly dropped by US forces in Vietnam; its name blends naphthenic and palmitic acids.

clue.text: A boring wet lefty

indicators.note: boring is drilling into something, so the letter A goes into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: moist means slightly wet

explanation.surface: A dull, feeble left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull, but here it means drilling into: A bores into MOIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Chairman Mao's communism is a left-winger, so a lefty in casual speech.

clue.text: Aren't diesel trains made to last?

indicators.note: to train is to shape or direct something, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about whether diesel locomotives are built to endure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' looks like the railway noun but is a verb signalling the anagram of AREN'T DIESEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To eternalise something is to make it everlasting, so made to last forever.

clue.text: Group receiving right fare

indicators.note: receiving means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: a bunch is a group or cluster

explanation.surface: A group gets the correct ticket price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' suggests a ticket price; here it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare means food served, and this late-morning meal blends breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: Figure seizing hotel involved in fund-raiser

indicators.note: seizing means the first piece grips the second inside it

parts.note: ten is a number, a figure

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the word hotel is mixed up

explanation.surface: A personality takes over a hotel as part of a charity drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a celebrity, but it is a number; 'involved' signals the anagram ELETHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A telethon is a long television broadcast that raises money for charity; it blends television and marathon.

clue.text: Rude message arranged to include sign of affection

indicators.note: to include means the first piece takes the second within it

parts.note: something arranged is set
X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A cheeky text set out with a kiss in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sext is a sexually explicit text message, blending sex and text.

clue.text: What's always very cool way to follow hairstyles

indicators.note: to follow means the second piece goes after the first

parts.note: a perm and an Afro are two hairstyles
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A cool way of keeping up with the latest hairdos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very cool' sounds like fashionable praise but means literally frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: Permafrost is ground that stays frozen all year round; it blends permanent and frost.

clue.text: Left chap kind of cross about English classification of the across solutions?

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a man is a chap

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a tau cross is T-shaped

explanation.surface: A sailor puzzles over a cross and English.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the theme: every across entry is a blend of two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau word fuses parts of two words, and each across entry here is one such blend.

clue.text: During work, drops greasy product

indicators.note: during puts one piece in the middle of the other, as an event within a period

parts.note: toil is hard work
rain falls in drops

explanation.surface: A greasy substance drips out while you work.
explanation.definitionFit: Train oil is oil rendered from whale blubber, an oily product once used in lamps.

clue.text: Drive in range, with ball cutting in

parts.note: ambit is scope or range

indicators.note: cutting means the ball piece slices into the middle of the other

parts.note: O has the round shape of a ball

explanation.surface: A golfer's drive on the range, with the ball sliced in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' and 'range' suggest golf; drive here is personal determination.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambition is a strong desire to succeed, the same as having drive.

clue.text: Beating cheers up hard little boy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means those letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils
Rob is a short form of the boy's name Robert

explanation.surface: Applause lifts a tough young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Something throbbing is pulsing, beating rhythmically, as in a heart athrob.

clue.text: Second sort of wine is sour

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
rosé is a pink wine

explanation.surface: A second kind of wine has gone sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy, as a sour mood is.

clue.text: Guy with pet, one with leg break

parts.note: a guy is a stay, a rope bracing a tent or mast
a cat is a pet
I is the Roman numeral one
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A man with his pet and someone with a broken leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg break' looks like an injury or a cricket delivery, but 'leg' is ON and 'break' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A staycation is a holiday at home rather than abroad, a break blending stay and vacation.

clue.text: Chatter about current leader with a stammer on the rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters run upwards, reading from the bottom

parts.note: re means concerning, about
Theresa May was then the UK leader; a stammer repeats her first letter, M-May

explanation.surface: Talk about a prime minister whose stutter is getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was Prime Minister of the UK when this appeared in 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to talk loudly and persistently, to chatter on.

clue.text: Not a single compiler scoffed

parts.note: no means not a single, as in no money
Shed is a Guardian crossword setter

explanation.surface: No crossword setter ate anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed is a compiler of Guardian cryptics; 'No' is also the cricket call refusing a single run.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is slang for food, so noshed means ate greedily, scoffed.

clue.text: Speaker pens line, about to publish online

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole is read backwards
pens means the first piece encloses the second, as an animal in a pen

parts.note: gob is slang for mouth, the part that speaks

explanation.surface: A speaker writes a line, about to post it online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'about to', but it turns GOLB around.
explanation.definitionFit: To blog is to write and post entries on a website; the word blends web and log.

clue.text: British country church, in which men bond

parts.note: Oman is a country in Arabia
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A British country church where men forge friendships.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromance is a close friendship between two men, blending brother and romance.

clue.text: Porridge maybe in breakfasts it complements

indicators.note: in means the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Porridge goes well with breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: PORRIDGE is a British TV comedy about prison life, not the oat dish the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is an example of a situation comedy, a word blending situation and comedy.

clue.text: Political crisis took hold, overwhelming monarch

indicators.note: overwhelming means the first piece engulfs the second

parts.note: bit is the past tense of bite, as brakes take hold
Rex is Latin for king, a monarch

explanation.surface: A political crisis took hold and swamped the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's departure from the EU caused prolonged political turmoil; the word blends British and exit.

clue.text: Ugly little creature welcomes electronic information about make-up

indicators.note: welcomes means the first piece takes the second in

parts.note: a gnome is a squat goblin-like creature
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A goblin greets electronic data about cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' suggests cosmetics but means genetic constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism's full set of genetic material is the data describing its constitution; it blends gene and chromosome.
